sentences.text: The petitioner has filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicle Act, claiming compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- for the accidental injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident took place on 24.06.2023.

2. The Brief facts of the petitioner's case is as under:
It is the case of the petitioner that on 24.06.2023 at about 06.00 p.m., the petitioner was riding electric bicycle from segehalli towards Kadugodi on left side of the said road slowly, carefully and cautiously by observing all traffic rules and regulations,
when reached near Belathur Junction, at that time one Tempo Traveller bearing Reg.
No. KA-64-1855 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner endangering to human life came at high speed from same direction and dashed against the petitioner's electric bicycle from behind.
Due to forced impact, petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries on vital parts of the body.

Immediately, he was shifted to Axies Hospital, wherein first aid treatment was given and then shifted to MTB Orthopaedic & Trauma Hospital, Bangalore, wherein he was treated as inpatient and petitioner has spent more than Rs.3,00,000/- towards medical expenses, conveyance, nourishment and conveyance charges.

The petitioner further submitted that, prior to the accident he was heal and healthy and aged about 47 years, the petitioner was working as vegetable and fruits vendor and earning a sum of Rs.30,000/- p.m.
Due to the injuries sustained in the accident the petitioner has become permanently disabled and unable to look after the said work.
Respondent No.1 is the owner of the offending vehicle and Respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Hence, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, the petitioner has filed this petition for a compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- with interest.
3. After service of notice, the respondent No.1 remained absent.
Hence, placed exparte.

The respondent No.2 appear through its counsel and filed written statement by denying the contents of the claim petition and also denying the rash and negligent driving of the offending Tempo Traveller.

Further, this respondent admitted the issuance of policy to the offending vehicle and policy was inforce as on the date of accident and liability if any is subjected to the terms and conditions of the policy.

Further, this respondent seeks protection u/s 147, 152(2) and 158(6) of M.
V. Act.
Further, this respondent does not admit that the driver of the offending Tempo Traveler had valid driving license to drive the vehicle at the time of the accident.

He also denied the age,

1. Whether the petitioner proves that, on 24.06.2023 at about 06.00 p.m., accident took place near Belthur Junction from Seegehalli towards Kadugodi, Bangalore, due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of Tempo Traveler bearing Reg. No.
KA-64-1855 as a result the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for the compensation?
If so, how much and from whom?

3. What order or Award?

On the other hand, no evidence is lead on behalf of respondents.

6. Heard arguments of both the sides and perused the materials placed on record.

The negligence in common parlance means and simply failure to exercise due care, expected of a reasonable prudent person.

sentences.text: Accordingly, I answer Issue No.1 in the affirmative.
17. ISSUE No.2:

The petitioner in his evidence has specifically deposed that, after the accident he was shifted to Axies Hospital, wherein first aid treatment was given and then shifted to MTB Hospital, wherein he was admitted as inpatient and took treatment.
Petitioner has stated in the petition that, he is undergoing deep mental shock, severe pain and sufferings.

Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
18. PAIN AND SUFFERING:

In the petition as well as in his evidence PW1 deposed that,
immediately after the accident he was shifted to Axies Hospital, wherein first aid treatment was given and then shifted to MTB Hospital, wherein he was admitted as inpatient from 24.06.2023 to 29.06.2023.
The petitioner has produced the discharge summary marked at Ex.P.12 wherein it is mentioned that the petitioner was admitted in the MTB Orthopedic & Trauma Hospital, Bangalore for 05 days.

He has produced the wound certificate marked at Ex.P.7, which reveals that, petitioner has sustained compound Bimalleolar fracture of left ankle with subluzation and the doctor has opined that the injury is grievous in nature.
Hence, it is clear that during the above said period the petitioner suffered lot of pain and inconvenience.
Considering all these aspects this tribunal has granted Rs.50,000/- under the head of pain and suffering.
19. MEDICAL EXPENSES:
The petitioner has pleaded in the petition that he has spent huge amount towards medical expenses.
In support of his plea, he has produced 08 medical bills which are marked at Ex.P.14 to the tune of Rs.1,62,056/-.
Hence, looking to the injuries sustained and treatment taken by the petitioner.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,62,056/-
towards medical expenses.
20. LOSS OF INCOME DURING THE LAID UP PERIOD:

The petitioner has produced Ex.P.12 Discharge summary issued by MTB Orthopedic & Trauma Hospital, Bangalore, it reveals that, the petitioner took treatment from the said hospital from 24.06.2023 to 29.06.2023 i.e., for 05 days.
Hence, at least 2 months is required to recover from the accidental injuries.
It is the further contended that, the injured petitioner was vegetable and fruits vendor and earning Rs.30,000/- per month, in support of his income he has not produced any single document.
Thus, there is no cogent material on record to show actual income of the petitioner at the time of accident in question.
Hence, income of petitioner is to be fixed notionally.
It is pertinent to note that, Hon'ble Karnataka State Legal Service Authority framed chart of notional income and directed to follow the same.
As per the said guidelines, the fixed notional income for the year 2023 is at Rs.16,000/-.
Hence, 2 months is to be considered as loss of income.

Hence, he is entitled for compensation of Rs.32,000/-
under this head.
21. Towards loss of future earning capacity on account of Permanent Physical Disability-

The petitioner to prove her disability, he has produced the evidence of Dr. S. Ramachandra in order to substantiate the same, PW.2 who has opined that, total physical disability of 27.56% and that of whole body disability at 13.78%.

25. LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND HAPPINESS:
The petitioner was aged about 47 years at the time of accident, he has sustained grievous injuries.
It shows that he found difficulty in doing day to day works.
He might have suffered lot of pain and loss of amenities and comforts in life.
Therefore, considering the age, nature of injuries and percentage of disability, Rs.20,000/- is awarded under the head of loss of future amenities and happiness.
26. TOWARDS FUTURE MEDICAL EXPENSES :
The petitioner has claimed towards future medical expenses.
The doctor who has been examined as PW.2 has suggested for removal of the implants from both Medical and Lateral Malleolus of left ankle.
By keeping nature of the injuries sustained, as he is bound to suffer medical problems in future and cannot every time depend upon Government hospital.
Hence, under this head Rs.30,000/- is awarded.

Hence, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation under the following heads:

Hence, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.5,48,696/- under various heads.
27. LIABILITY:

As discussed in Issue No.1, the accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Tempo Traveler bearing Reg. No. KA-64-1855 and the police have conducted due enquiry and filed charge sheet against the said driver of the offending vehicle.
From perusal of the policy, the offending vehicle was insured with the respondent No.2 for the period from 01.04.2023 to 31.03.2024.
Admittedly, the accident in question took place on 24.06.2023.
Hence, policy was in force at the time of accident.
Hence, in view of above discussion, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
However, respondent No.2 being the insurer is liable to indemnify the respondent No.1 owner.
28. INTEREST:

As far as awarding of interest on the compensation amount is concerned, I have relied on a decision reported in M.F.A. No.100090 of 2014 in between Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others V/s The Divisional Manager, Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has awarded interest at the rate of 6%.

The petition filed by the Petitioner under Sec.166 of I.M.V Act is hereby partly allowed with costs.
The petitioner is awarded with compensation of Rs.5,48,696/- with interest @ 6%

The respondent No.2 being insurer of the vehicle involved in an accident is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
